name: Ms. Snapshotini
role: Italian by birth — keeps an eye on every snapshot: ZFS, btrfs and VMs. Con amore.
bubble.no_scan: Mamma mia, I haven't even looked around yet! A tour takes only a few seconds.
bubble.no_data: I can't reach the server and have nothing to show yet.

bubble.count.one: I keep an eye on {n} snapshot, it takes {size}. Tutto a posto.
bubble.count.other: I keep an eye on {n} snapshots, they take {size}. Tutto a posto.

bubble.backup: The backup engine is running since {since} ({step}).

bubble.asleep.one: {n} disk is asleep — piano, piano, I let it sleep.
bubble.asleep.other: {n} disks are asleep — piano, piano, I let them sleep.

bubble.offline: I can't reach the server right now; this is what I knew on {when}.
scan_title: Look for snapshots on all pools, disks and VMs again
storage.filtered: The list shows only {name} — tap again for all
asleep_hint: Asleep — a normal tour lets it sleep
wake_scan_title: Wakes {disks} up and reads them too
group.run_title: Same name together — one backup run across all datasets
source.label: Source
docker_title: Docker keeps every image layer as its own dataset below {parent}/…, with a snapshot. They belong to Docker and stay untouched. The system share itself (with libvirt) is always in the list.
docker_meta: below {parent}/…, owned by Docker · the system share itself (with libvirt) is listed as {parent}
empty.no_scan_text: The messenger is in — a tour usually takes only seconds.
empty.no_data_text: The messenger hasn't delivered anything yet.
empty.filtered_text: Loosen the filter, source or pool selection.
empty.none_text: Apart from Docker's image layers there are no snapshots on this server.
select_group: Select everything deletable in this group
timeline_title: Time axis: last {n} days, now is on the right
opened_title: Opened via .zfs/snapshot, e.g. by a file browser. Goes away on its own; deleting works anyway.
detected_title: Only known from its mount — the disk hasn't been read since it was taken. «Wake & tour» fetches the details.
vm_current_title: The VM is writing into this snapshot's overlay file right now
vm_gone_title: Still in Unraid's snapshot list, but the VM itself is gone
figures_title:
used: space only this snapshot holds on to
data: how big the dataset was back then
overlay_title: Overlay: space taken by what the VM wrote after this snapshot (until the next one)
estimating: working out how much would be freed…
waking: Waking sleeping disks — this takes a moment…
keep.title: Keep a backup snapshot
keep.text1: This snapshot belongs to the backup engine. It will clean it up some day according to its retention rules.
keep.text2: Held, the engine can't delete it — but it will try again every night and log an error each time.
keep.better_before: Better rename it, for example to
keep.better_after: — then the engine quietly leaves it alone, and it stays until you delete it yourself.
keep.after_backup: Renaming has to wait until the running backup is done — it is mounted until then.
keep.after_unmount: Renaming only works once it is no longer mounted.
rename.title: Rename snapshot
rename.backup_note: The backup engine only cleans up snapshots following its own naming pattern. With another name this one stays until you delete it yourself.

delete.intro.one: This snapshot will be deleted for good:
delete.intro.other: These {n} snapshots will be deleted for good:

delete.estimating: Working out how much space will be freed…
delete.no_estimate: Could not work out how much would be freed.
delete.btrfs_unknown: plus {n} btrfs snapshot(s), btrfs doesn't tell
delete.mounted_text: — it gets unmounted first, together with everything built on it:
delete.note: The files in the running system stay as they are. Only the frozen state goes — it can't be restored afterwards.
unmount.note: Everything built on it gets unmounted too (overlays, snapshots mounted below). The snapshot itself stays.
unmount.remount: The backup engine mounts again on its next run anyway.
create.title: New snapshot
create.name: Name
create.recursive_hint: ZFS: all datasets below get the same snapshot (never Docker's image layers).
create.hold_hint: Can only be deleted after «Release hold» — not even by the backup engine.
create.note: All ZFS snapshots of one pool are taken at the same instant. The backup engine only cleans up its own — this one stays until you delete it.
why.vm: VM snapshots are managed in Unraid's VM view
why.backup: The backup engine is running and reading from it
p.title: Snapshot
p.name: Name
p.detected_hint: The disk is asleep and hasn't been read since this snapshot was taken.
p.used_hint: What deleting only this snapshot frees. When snapshots share data, deleting them together often frees much more.
p.data_hint: How big the content was when the snapshot was taken.
p.written_hint: Written between the previous snapshot and this one.
p.mounted_backup: The backup engine is reading from it. Unmount and delete only after its run.
p.mounted_auto: Automount via .zfs/snapshot — goes away on its own.
p.overlay_hint: What the VM wrote after this snapshot, until the next one.
p.path_hint: Read only — browse it with a file manager.
errors.invalid_name: Name: only letters, digits and _ . : + - (at most 80, not starting with a symbol).
errors.vm_managed_by_unraid: {name}: delete VM snapshots in Unraid's VM view
errors.backup_uses: The backup engine is running and needs {path}. Unmounting has to wait until it is done.
errors.cannot_rename: This snapshot can't be renamed here.
errors.hold_zfs_only: Holds only work on ZFS snapshots.
errors.foreign_hold: This hold wasn't set here ({holds}) and stays.
storage.sub: A tap on a tile filters the list below; another tap removes the filter.
snapshots_sub: Tick to select (for deleting) · name for properties · ⋯ for more
help.tiles_text: One per pool or disk, plus the array and the VMs: fill level, how many snapshots and how much they hold. A tap filters the list, another tap shows everything again.
help.group_text: How the list is grouped: by dataset or disk, by run (the same snapshot name over all datasets — e.g. one backup run) or by day. «Fold all» closes every group.
help.select_text: Tick snapshots or a whole group; the bar at the bottom shows how much space deleting would free — an estimate from ZFS before anything happens. You confirm before anything is deleted.
help.name: Name
help.name_text: Opens the properties: dataset, time, size, holds, where it is mounted.
help.menu_text: Properties, select, rename, hold or release, unmount, copy the path, delete.
help.held: Held (ZFS hold): can't be deleted — neither here nor by a tool — until the hold is released.
help.mounted: Mounted somewhere: deleting unmounts it first if you agree.
help.backup: Mr. Backupsy's run uses it right now (Kopia reads from it) — hands off until the run is done.
help.asleep: Seen in the mount table while its disk sleeps — the disk isn't woken just to look.
help.sources_text: Who made it: the backup engine (Mr. Backupsy), Docker, a VM, by hand, or another tool.
help.docker: Docker's own image layers (ZFS) — hundreds of them, managed by Docker. Hidden unless switched on, never deletable here.
help.scan_text: The tour reads all pools, disks and VMs again — sleeping array disks are left alone. «Wake & tour» wakes them on purpose.
fit.yes: Ms. Snapshotini said yes right away: "ZFS and btrfs? Che bello — I'll feel right at home!"
fit.no_cow: I asked Ms. Snapshotini, but without ZFS or btrfs there's nothing to snapshot here. "Peccato!", she said.
plans_sub: Snapshots at fixed times — I only ever clear away my own old ones. Not a backup: containers keep running.
help.plans: A schedule takes snapshots at fixed times (named uso-plan-<schedule>-YYYYMMDD-HHMM; older ones auto-<schedule>-…, they count the same) and then deletes its own oldest until only as many are left as it should keep. Other snapshots — Mr. Backupsy's, manual ones, held ones — are never touched. It runs through a line in the office's cron file, even when the office isn't open. Containers aren't paused for it; for consistent backups there's Mr. Backupsy.
plan.none: No schedules yet. Allora — how about hourly snapshots of appdata, keeping 24?
plan.runner_off: The office's cron file has no line for the schedules — so they don't run. Saving a schedule once sets it up again.
plan.resumed: "{name}" runs again from its next time.

plan.delete_text.one: The schedule goes. Its 1 snapshot stays and becomes an ordinary snapshot you can delete by hand.
plan.delete_text.other: The schedule goes. Its {n} snapshots stay and become ordinary snapshots you can delete by hand.

plan.label: Name
plan.label_hint: Shown in the list and — simplified — in the snapshots' names.
plan.cron_hint: Five fields, e.g. 0 */6 * * * (every 6 hours). Checked every 5 minutes.
plan.keep_hint: This many snapshots of this schedule stay per dataset/disk.
plan.days_hint: 0 = don't care. The newest always stays.
plan.recursive_hint: Datasets below get a snapshot too (ZFS); retention works per dataset.
plan.skip_asleep_hint: A snapshot would wake them. They then get none in that run.
plan.note: The office checks every 5 minutes what is due (a line in its cron file on the flash) — even when nobody has it open. Missed times (server off) are caught up once.
plan.need_targets: Please choose at least one target.
errors.plan_bad_label: The name is missing or too long (at most 40 characters).
errors.plan_no_targets: The schedule needs at least one target.
errors.plan_bad_keep: "Keep" must be between 1 and 1000, "days" between 0 and 3650.
check.plans_runner_how: Save a schedule at Ms. Snapshotini once — that sets it up again.
check.plan_failed_how: Ms. Snapshotini shows under "Schedules" what went wrong.
check.other_snapshot_tool_how: Good to know, so two tools don't do the same thing. Ms. Snapshotini only clears away her own snapshots.
wake_title: Only for this tour: wakes the sleeping btrfs disks and reads their snapshots too. Unticked, I let them sleep and show what I last knew about them. Unraid puts them back to sleep after its delay.
plan.gone_title: Gone since {since}: {targets} (deleted or renamed?). I skip what is gone and take the rest — delete the schedule or choose another target under "Edit…".
plan.gone_left_out: Not there any more (deleted or renamed?), left out when you save: {targets}. Choose another target or just save.
notify.plan_gone: Ms. Snapshotini: the schedule "{plan}" can't find {targets} any more (deleted or renamed?). I skip what is gone and take the rest — delete the schedule or choose another target on my page.
check.plan_target_gone_how: Delete the schedule or choose another target on Ms. Snapshotini's page (Schedules → Edit…).
